title: Some remarks on the connection between generative diffusion and optimal transport
abstract: arXiv:2610.13614v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We discuss three simple connections between generative diffusion and optimal transport. First, the joint law of the data and of their Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noising is, at every time, the solution of an entropic optimal-transport problem, at a temperature set by the noise level. Backward diffusion can consequently be read as an annealing which gradually decreases the entropic regularization. Second, we study the speciation transition--how the modes of the data distribution emerge during generation--and compare how it happens in diffusion and flow matching with respect to optimal transport. Using Gaussian mixtures as high-dimensional example, we show that the dynamical instability through which diffusion and flow matching separate the modes becomes, for optimal transport, an exponentially thin boundary layer at the beginning of generation, which is rounded by entropic regularization. Third, considering a generic forward dynamics with a gene

translated_title: 关于生成扩散与最优传输之间联系的一些注记
translated_abstract: 我们讨论了生成扩散与最优传输之间的三个简单联系。首先，数据与其 Ornstein-Uhlenbeck 加噪过程的联合分布在每一时刻都是某个熵正则化最优传输问题的解，其温度由噪声水平决定。因此，反向扩散可以被解读为一种逐渐降低熵正则化的退火过程。其次，我们研究了物种形成转变（speciation transition）——即数据分布的各个模式在生成过程中如何浮现——并比较了它在扩散模型、流匹配与最优传输中的发生方式。以高斯混合分布作为高维例子，我们表明扩散与流匹配借以分离各模式的动力学不稳定性，在最优传输情形下变为生成初始阶段一个指数级薄的边界层，而该边界层会被熵正则化所平滑。第三，考虑一个带有一般前向动力学的……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文揭示了生成扩散与最优传输之间的三个简单联系：数据加噪的联合分布在每个时刻都是熵正则化最优传输问题的解（因此反向扩散等价于逐渐降低熵正则化的退火过程），且扩散与流匹配中分离数据模式的动力学不稳定性，在最优传输中表现为生成初期一个被熵正则化平滑的指数级薄边界层。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes three simple connections between generative diffusion and optimal transport: the joint law of data and their OU-noising solves an entropic optimal transport problem at every time (so backward diffusion is an annealing that gradually decreases the entropic regularization), and the dynamical instability by which diffusion and flow matching separate data modes becomes, under optimal transport, an exponentially thin boundary layer at the beginning of generation that is smoothed by entropic regularization.
